text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Deputy Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong says that opposition ward Hougang will not be part of Ang Mo Kio Community Development Council.
- Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong and Hongkong's future chief executive Tung Chee Hwa renew old friendship at meeting in Hong Kong.
- Lift at Textile Centre in Jalan Sultan plunges 19 storeys, hurting seven people.
- Share investors' cautious mood causes trading on Singapore bourse to fall to its lowest level so far this year in April.

- CAM International Holdings issues statement assuring shareholders that it is unaware of any serious offences involving fraud or dishonesty committed against the company by any of its officers or employees.
- Business performance and sentiment remain weak in first quarter of this year but situation could be turning around.
- Singaporeans among most-heavily banked people in the world, going by the number of bank branches and automated teller machines.
- Sesdaq's market capitalisation has risen nearly Singapore $1.5 billion in four months.
- Shell Tower gets new name as Singapore Land Tower from July 1.
